beats.text: You know what's underrated? Compliments. I give them freely. 'Nice coat.' 'Lovely teeth.' 'Great posture for a mortal.'
I'm working on it. The kindness. Every day. Six hundred years of practice and I still surprise myself.
My therapist says I should acknowledge the urge without becoming it. I said, 'doc, I've BEEN it. For centuries. I'm auditioning for something else.'
And then I saw my reflection in the spoon. And the reflection winked FIRST., I didn't tell my therapist that part. She has a nice face. I don't want to worry her.
So now I compliment the reflection too. 'Nice coat.' It says nothing back. That's progress. Monologues are just compliments with nowhere to land.
Being good is a practice, not a destination. The destination is probably a blood bank. But the practice! The practice is soup and goats and compliments to spoons. See you Tuesday.
